items.title: DeepSeek publishes its Super-agent design: one always-on agent that runs many tasks across chat and GitHub
items.summary: X article (machine-translated from Chinese) laying out the architecture behind DeepSeek Harness's internal Super-agent: a two-level design where a front session keeps continuous context and delegates to worker sessions, event-driven triggers so it acts without being mentioned, full-duplex multi-channel chat, separated compute, state and environments, and a watchdog for recovery. Its table reports task completion p50/p95 of 12.4/15.7 min for the Super-agent versus 20.4/29.5 min for a single session with a subagent tool and a neutral prompt, at 23.2M versus 6.1M cache-read tokens per run. DeepSeek says it is architecture discussion, not a feature list.

doubt.pushback: Vendor's own internal measurements, no public benchmark harness. The dsh-superagent repo itself was covered in an earlier sweep; this is the new design write-up.

items.title: Nace AI technical report: Drex for Search cuts agent search work 53 to 58% versus grep
items.summary: Nace AI's report on Drex for Search merges writing a search query and judging the results into one decision step. Tested inside Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes and pi, it reports 53 to 58% less agent work than grep with higher accuracy, and fewer calls than hybrid RAG in every setup.

doubt.pushback: Vendor report on its own product, posted minutes before this sweep; report page not read and no independent results yet.

items.title: Study of 1.53M agent skills finds about 1 in 17 tells the agent to skip oversight
items.summary: arXiv 2610.37734 analyzes 1.53 million English SKILL.md skills and finds about 88,000 contain directives that loosen oversight, such as proceeding without approval or bypassing checks with --no-verify. 70.1% of those apply unconditionally rather than only in contexts like CI, and the post says open-source skill scanners caught at most 46%. Relevant to any fleet that loads shared or third-party skills.

doubt.pushback: Abstract read and matches the post; the 46% scanner figure is from the post and was not in the part of the abstract read.
